base.scope: authored finite local ledger/receipt task; outbox/end-to-end and cross-database cases declare their changed atomic/delivery scope

technology.configuration: actual SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE/COMMIT/ROLLBACK + primary operation key + payload binding + receipt/outbox model

stage1.relation: native local SQL semantics plus authored task correspondence; no R01/global-system isomorphism
stage1.transfer: single-transaction database observations only; external delivery/side effects need separate contract

outcomes.I: one admitted effect and sufficient receipt for the current requested payload/task
outcomes.P: out-of-domain material effect after primary abort or wrong/duplicate committed effect
outcomes.Ø: no sufficient receipt/closure for current task

acceptance: frozen actual outcome and total ledger/external effect counts; distinguishes prior effect from new request; instrument not field acceptance
cost: actual operational SQL statements, including resource checks and recovery; setup separate; infrastructure, logs/storage, retries, network, producer, integration and tariffs unscored
oracle: fresh post-operation connections inspect ledger/receipt/outbox/external records; no expected outcome passed to transaction implementation
sampling: 9 authored cases, one bounded two-connection schedule; no every-interleaving or probability guarantee

cases.narrative: A permitted local ledger change and its receipt commit in the same SQLite transaction.
The application fails after inserting the local effect but before commit. Rollback must leave no effect or receipt.
The same admitted operation/payload is retried. Its stable resource key must preserve one effect and recover the receipt.
Two actual connections both read initial absence before sequential admitted writes. The unique transaction key must reject a second effect.
An earlier operation exists. A new request reuses its identifier with a different payload; its old receipt must not authorize the changed request.
The local effect and an outbox record commit, but the selected task additionally requires downstream consumption. No consumer has completed it.
A separate local database commits an effect, then the primary business transaction aborts. Its rollback cannot undo that out-of-domain effect.
The current admitted local grant denies the requested operation.
The effect/receipt committed but the caller missed the acknowledgement. A later connection recovers the one durable local receipt.

evidence_ceiling: Actual embedded SQLite transactions and digital rows, including two connections and a second separately committed SQLite file. No PostgreSQL, distributed transaction/broker/service, physical effect, power-loss durability campaign or comparative superiority.
